مَسْفُوحٌ : see سَافِحٌ. ―
-b2- [Hence,] applied to a camel, it means قَدْ سُفِحَ فِى الأَرْضِ وَمُدَّ (assumed tropical:) [Stretched, or extended, upon the ground; وَمُدَّ being an explicative adjunct]. (K.) ―
-b3- (assumed tropical:) Wide. (K.) You say نَاقَةٌ مَسْفُوحَةُ الإِبْطِ (tropical:) A she-camel wide in the arm-pit. (A, K.) And جَمَلٌ مَسْفُوحُ الضُّلُوعِ (tropical:) A camel [wide i. e.] not contracted in the ribs. (A, TA.) ―
-b4- (assumed tropical:) Thick, coarse, or big. (K.) ―
-b5- You say also, إِنَّهُ لَمَسْفُوحُ العُنُقِ, meaning (assumed tropical:) Verily he is long, and thick, coarse, or big, in the neck. (TA.) ―
-b6- And المَسْفُوحُ is the name of (assumed tropical:) A horse of Sakhr Ibn-'Amr Ibn-El-Hárith. (K.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
